name: Bakgabun (Park's powder)

lead: Bakgabun, meaning Park's powder, was Korea's first mass-produced cosmetic and first face powder. Launched in the mid-1910s, it was affordable and widely sold, and it let women achieve the smooth, pale complexion that fit the aesthetic of the time.

Its history is also a cautionary tale about ingredients: the formula contained lead, which helped the powder cling to skin but was later reported to damage it. Sales dropped and lead-free powders from Korean makers followed.

paras: It was a loose face powder applied to the face to lighten and even the skin tone. It sold across Korea during its peak, and copies such as Seogabun and Janggabun appeared quickly under similar family-name branding.

Lead-containing cosmetics are associated with skin damage and with lead absorption. Historical accounts say the powder's lead content caused skin problems, which contributed to its fall from favour; modern cosmetics regulation restricts lead. It is a historical product and is not on the market today.

web.title: The changing face of Korean makeup (Korea JoongAng Daily)

chain: Apply loose white powder to the face
Period ideal of beauty for women in early 20th-century Korea
angle.text: The powder was a daily complexion product, applied to even and brighten the face. Its history shows how ingredient safety shaped later cosmetics.

lead: Bakgabun, literally Park's powder, was the first mass-produced cosmetic in Korea and the country's first face powder, sold as a bestseller from 1916 to 1930.[1] The JoongAng Daily dates its creation to 1916.[2]

For appearance, it offered an inexpensive way to even and lighten the face. A curator quoted by the Korea JoongAng Daily said that at the height of the boom it sold more than 50,000 products a day.[2]

The powder contained lead, used to make it stick to the skin, and the same curator said it harmed the skin of users.[2] Sales fell sharply and similar products appeared, followed by Korean makers developing lead-free powders.[1][2]

paras: Wikipedia describes Bakgabun as Korea's first mass-produced cosmetic and first face powder and says it was a bestseller from 1916 to 1930.[1] A Korea JoongAng Daily article dates its creation to 1916 and says it was affordable and widely available, with imitations such as Janggabun appearing.[2]
Accounts of the exact launch year and of when it left the market vary between sources, so specifics are not settled.

The formula used lead to help the powder adhere to skin. The curator Lee Ji-sun said this damaged women's skin, and the product lost favour almost as quickly as it had risen once the lead content became known.[2] Wikipedia notes sales dropped sharply and similar products were launched.[1]

timeline.event: Bakgabun is launched as Korea's first domestically produced face powder.[2]
End of the period in which it was a bestseller, according to Wikipedia.[1]
